title: asyncio — Asynchronous I/O
content: asyncio is a library to write concurrent code using the async/await syntax. It provides an event loop that runs coroutines and schedules tasks for high-performance network and I/O-bound code.

title: typing — Support for type hints
content: This module provides runtime support for type hints. You can annotate variables and function signatures so that static type checkers can verify your code.

title: dataclasses — Data Classes
content: The dataclasses module provides a decorator and functions for automatically adding generated special methods such as __init__ and __repr__ to user-defined classes.

title: Async IO in Python: A Complete Walkthrough
content: Learn asynchronous programming in Python using async and await. This tutorial walks through coroutines, the event loop, and awaiting concurrent tasks step by step.

title: PostgreSQL Indexes
content: Indexes are a common way to enhance database performance. An index lets the server find and retrieve specific rows much faster than scanning the whole table.

title: PostgreSQL Full Text Search
content: Full text search lets you query natural-language documents stored in the database using tsvector and tsquery, ranking results by relevance to the search terms.

title: Concurrency and async / await
content: FastAPI lets you write endpoint functions with async def. This page explains concurrency, the event loop, and when awaiting coroutines improves throughput for I/O-bound APIs.

title: Redis in-memory data store
content: Redis is an in-memory key-value store used as a cache, database, and message broker, serving hot data with sub-millisecond latency.

title: Docker images and containers
content: A Docker image is an immutable filesystem snapshot; a container is a running instance started from that image, isolating an application and its dependencies.

title: git merge
content: git merge joins two or more development histories together, combining the work from separate branches and recording the integration as a merge commit.
